prompt: What are the best email marketing platforms for a small business?

trials.response:
For a **typical small business in 2026**, I’d narrow the market to a handful of platforms rather than automatically defaulting to Mailchimp. Pricing and feature sets have changed quite a bit.

| Platform | Best suited to | Why it stands out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | **Most small businesses / best all-round starting point** | Very simple UI, newsletters, forms, landing pages, websites and automation in one product. Free up to 250 subscribers; Comfort starts around **$12/mo**. MailerLite |
| **Brevo** | **Budget-conscious businesses + multichannel marketing** | Email, SMS, transactional email, CRM-style tools and automation. Free tier allows 300 emails/day; Starter starts **$9/mo**, Standard **$18/mo** with full marketing automation. Brevo Help+1 |
| **Omnisend** | **Small ecommerce stores** | Built around Shopify/WooCommerce-style ecommerce, with abandoned-cart flows, product blocks, email/SMS and ecommerce automations. Paid plans start around **$16/mo**. Omnisend |
| **Klaviyo** | **Growing ecommerce businesses with lots of customer data** | Strong behavioral segmentation, product/customer data and sophisticated ecommerce lifecycle automation. More powerful—but usually more complex and expensive than what a very small business needs. Omnisend+1 |
| **Kit** | **Creators, newsletters, coaches and digital products** | Excellent tagging, subscriber funnels, landing pages and creator monetization. Its free plan supports up to **10,000 subscribers**, while the Creator plan adds unlimited visual automations and sequences. Kit |
| **Constant Contact** | **Local businesses wanting strong human support** | Straightforward email marketing plus social, events and extensive integrations. Lite starts around **$12/mo** and Standard around **$35/mo** before annual discounts. Constant Contact+1 |
| **Mailchimp** | Businesses already embedded in the Mailchimp ecosystem | Mature editor, integrations, analytics and automation, but I wouldn't choose it automatically on price/value alone today. Standard currently starts around **$20/mo** at the entry level shown on its pricing page. Mailchimp |

### What I'd shortlist

For a **normal service business, agency, local company, SaaS startup, consultant, clinic, etc.**, I'd start by testing **MailerLite vs. Brevo**.

**MailerLite** is especially attractive when you want something that a non-marketer can learn quickly. You get email campaigns, signup forms, automations, landing pages and even simple websites/digital products without stitching together many tools. MailerLite

**Brevo** becomes particularly compelling if you expect to use **email + transactional email + SMS + CRM/sales features**. Its pricing is also more send-volume-oriented than many traditional subscriber-count platforms. Brevo Help+1

For an **online store**, I'd compare **Omnisend and Klaviyo** instead. Omnisend is usually the easier SMB-oriented option; Klaviyo makes more sense when behavioral data, segmentation and sophisticated lifecycle marketing become central to the business. Omnisend+1

For a **newsletter/personal brand/course business**, I'd seriously consider **Kit** because its product is built around creators rather than conventional corporate marketing teams. Kit

**So the short version:**

**MailerLite — strongest general-purpose SMB option**

**Brevo — strong budget/multichannel option**

**Omnisend — ecommerce SMBs**

**Klaviyo — advanced ecommerce**

**Kit — creators/newsletters**

**Constant Contact — support-heavy/local businesses**

**Mailchimp — established all-rounder, but no longer an automatic first choice**

If you tell me **what kind of small business, number of contacts, and whether you need ecommerce/automation**, I can narrow those to the 2–3 that fit the use case instead of comparing features you probably won't use.

For most small businesses in 2026, I’d narrow the field to **MailerLite, Brevo, Mailchimp, Kit, Omnisend, and ActiveCampaign**. The right choice depends much more on your business model than on which platform has the longest feature list.

| Platform | Best for | Why it stands out | Main drawback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | Most small businesses | Simple, inexpensive, good automation, landing pages, forms, website tools | Less sophisticated than ActiveCampaign for complex CRM/automation |
| **Brevo** | Service businesses / CRM + email | Email, SMS, WhatsApp, transactional email and CRM in one ecosystem | Interface/workflows can feel less polished |
| **Mailchimp** | Beginners wanting a familiar brand | Easy templates, integrations, broad ecosystem | Can become expensive as contacts grow |
| **Kit** | Creators, newsletters, coaches | Excellent tagging, sequences, creator monetization | Less suited to traditional retail/business marketing |
| **Omnisend** | Ecommerce | Strong cart abandonment, product recommendations and store automations | Overkill for non-ecommerce companies |
| **ActiveCampaign** | Automation-heavy businesses | Deep segmentation, workflows, CRM integrations | More complexity and usually more cost |

### My default pick: MailerLite

For a typical small company that needs newsletters, lead capture, welcome sequences, landing pages and basic sales automation, **MailerLite is probably the best balance of price, usability and capability**.

Its current Comfort plan starts at **$12/month**, while the free tier supports up to **250 active subscribers and 2,500 emails/month**. MailerLite also includes forms, landing pages, visual automations, website tools, A/B testing and integrations. MailerLite+1

One thing to watch: MailerLite changed its plans on **June 16, 2026**, so older reviews mentioning a 500- or 1,000-subscriber free tier may no longer be accurate. MailerLite

### If you want CRM + multiple communication channels: Brevo

**Brevo** is particularly attractive for a service business because you're not just buying an email newsletter tool. It combines email marketing with transactional email, SMS, WhatsApp, automation and sales functionality.

Its current plans start at **$9/month for Starter** and **$18/month for Standard**. The free tier allows **300 sends per day** and storage of up to 100,000 contacts, although automation on Free is limited to 2,000 contacts. Brevo Help

The important distinction is that Brevo's pricing is much more oriented around **sending volume** than simply charging you for every contact you store. That can make it attractive if you maintain a large database but don't email everyone constantly.

### If you're running an online store: Omnisend

For Shopify/WooCommerce-style ecommerce, I'd look at **Omnisend before MailerLite**.

It has ecommerce-specific workflows for things like abandoned carts, post-purchase emails and product recommendations. Its Standard plan starts at **$16/month**, while its free tier allows 500 emails/month to up to 250 contacts. Omnisend Help Center+1

That ecommerce specialization is the reason I'd choose it over a general-purpose newsletter system for a store.

### If you're a creator/newsletter business: Kit

**Kit** is built around creators rather than conventional small businesses. It has strong tagging, subscriber segmentation, sequences, landing pages, paid newsletters and digital-product selling.

Interestingly, its current free plan supports **up to 10,000 subscribers**, while Creator is currently listed at **$33/month for 1,000 subscribers** when billed annually. Kit

So for a blogger, YouTuber, consultant, newsletter operator or digital-product creator, Kit can make much more sense than Mailchimp.

### ActiveCampaign is the automation powerhouse

If your requirements sound like:

> “When somebody downloads X, visits page Y twice, has tag Z, hasn't purchased in 14 days and has opened three emails, send them into another sequence and update the CRM.”

then you're entering **ActiveCampaign territory**.

Its current platform emphasizes multi-step automation, segmentation, CRM/ecommerce integrations, landing pages and increasingly AI-assisted marketing functionality. ActiveCampaign Help Center+1

For a very small company, though, I'd usually avoid starting there unless you genuinely need that complexity.

### And Mailchimp?

Mailchimp is still perfectly capable and has perhaps the most recognizable ecosystem. Its Essentials plan currently starts around **$13/month** and Standard around **$20/month** at the entry level displayed on its pricing page. Mailchimp

But for a new small business, I don't think its brand recognition alone is enough reason to choose it over MailerLite or Brevo. Costs and limits become important as your audience grows.

**So the practical shortlist is:**

-   **Normal small business → MailerLite**
    
-   **Services + CRM/SMS/WhatsApp → Brevo**
    
-   **Shopify/ecommerce → Omnisend**
    
-   **Creator/newsletter → Kit**
    
-   **Complex funnels/automation → ActiveCampaign**
    
-   **Want a huge ecosystem and already know Mailchimp → Mailchimp**
    

If I were launching a small business from zero today and had no special requirements, **I'd start with MailerLite**, and only move to something more specialized once the business model demanded it.

As of **September 2026**, there isn’t one email platform that is best for every small business. The strongest choices depend on whether you mainly need newsletters, automation, e-commerce, or a CRM.

| Platform | Best for | Why I'd consider it | Main drawback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | **Best overall for most small businesses** | Clean interface, strong newsletter builder, landing pages, forms, automations, websites and digital products without excessive complexity | Its free plan was reduced in June 2026 to **250 subscribers / 2,500 emails per month**. MailerLite+1 |
| **Brevo** | **Best value / larger contact database** | Email + transactional email + SMS, with WhatsApp/chat capabilities; free plan stores up to **100,000 contacts** and allows **300 emails/day** | Daily sending limit on free plan; interface isn't as polished as MailerLite for pure newsletter creation. Brevo Help |
| **Kit** | **Best for creators, newsletters and digital products** | Extremely generous free tier: **up to 10,000 subscribers**, unlimited broadcasts, forms and landing pages; built around creator monetization | Advanced sequences and visual automations require paid Creator plans. Kit+1 |
| **Klaviyo** | **Best for Shopify/e-commerce** | Excellent customer segmentation, purchase/event data, revenue attribution and automated e-commerce flows | Usually overkill for a simple newsletter; free tier is only **250 active profiles / 500 sends monthly**. Klaviyo UK+1 |
| **ActiveCampaign** | **Best for advanced automation** | Much deeper conditional automation, segmentation, CRM/e-commerce integrations and customer journeys than most basic newsletter tools | More complexity and cost; pricing starts around **$15/month for under 1,000 contacts**. ActiveCampaign+1 |
| **HubSpot** | **Best if CRM + sales + marketing must live together** | Email sits alongside CRM, leads, sales pipelines, forms and customer data | Can become dramatically more expensive once you require Professional marketing functionality; Professional currently starts around **$800/month** on annual billing. HubSpot |
| **Mailchimp** | Established general-purpose option | Mature ecosystem, lots of integrations, templates and widespread third-party support | Its free plan is now quite limited: **250 contacts and 500 monthly sends**. Mailchimp+1 |

### What I'd choose

For a **normal small business—consulting, agency, clinic, local service, SaaS, etc.—I'd start with MailerLite**. It strikes a good balance between simplicity and serious functionality without forcing you into an enterprise-style marketing stack.

If keeping costs extremely low while building a large contact database matters, **Brevo** becomes especially interesting. If you're building a **newsletter/content business**, I'd take **Kit** instead. For **Shopify or another e-commerce store**, I'd use **Klaviyo**. And if the business depends heavily on sophisticated lead nurturing—_clicked X → visited pricing → didn't purchase → wait 2 days → branch based on behavior → notify sales_—I'd look at **ActiveCampaign**.

One notable change is that **MailerLite and Mailchimp are no longer particularly generous free options**. MailerLite cut its free subscriber limit from 500 to 250 on **June 16, 2026**, while Kit currently allows up to 10,000 subscribers on its free plan. MailerLite+1

So my practical shortlist would be **MailerLite, Brevo, Kit, Klaviyo and ActiveCampaign**. Mailchimp is still perfectly usable, but for a brand-new small business I wouldn't automatically choose it just because it's the most familiar name.

For a typical small business in **2026**, I’d shortlist **MailerLite, Brevo, Mailchimp, Klaviyo, Kit, and Constant Contact**. They overlap, but they’re optimized for different businesses.

| Platform | Best for | Starting point | Main strength | Main drawback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | Most small businesses | Free; paid from about **$12/mo** | Excellent balance of automation, landing pages, forms, templates and price | Smaller ecosystem than Mailchimp |
| **Brevo** | Businesses with larger contact lists / multichannel marketing | Free; Starter from **$9/mo** | Email + SMS + WhatsApp + CRM-style features; pricing is heavily send-volume based | Interface/analytics can feel less polished |
| **Mailchimp** | Businesses wanting a mature ecosystem | Free to 250 contacts; Essentials from **$13/mo**, Standard about **$20/mo** | Strong integrations, templates, segmentation and automation | Can become expensive as contacts grow |
| **Klaviyo** | **Shopify/e-commerce** | Free tier available | Very strong customer segmentation, ecommerce triggers and revenue-focused automation | Usually unnecessary for a simple newsletter business |
| **Kit** | Creators, newsletters, courses, digital products | Free up to **10,000 subscribers**; Creator about **$33/mo** at 1,000 subscribers | Excellent tagging, sequences and creator monetization | Less suited to traditional local businesses |
| **Constant Contact** | Local businesses, associations, events | From about **$12/mo** | Very beginner-friendly, good human support and event/social tools | Automation/value isn't as strong as MailerLite/Brevo |

Prices and limits vary with subscribers and sending volume. Current official pricing confirms MailerLite's free tier and paid plans from around $12, Brevo from $9, Mailchimp Essentials from $13 and Standard from $20, Kit's unusually large free creator plan, and Constant Contact's entry pricing around $12. ### What I'd choose

**For most small businesses → MailerLite.**

This is probably the strongest starting point if you want newsletters, signup forms, landing pages and automated sequences without paying for a complicated marketing suite. Its paid plans include features such as automation, testing, AI-assisted writing, ecommerce tracking and integrations. MailerLite

**If you're extremely price-sensitive → Brevo.**

It's especially interesting if you may collect lots of contacts but don't email every person constantly. Brevo also combines email, SMS, WhatsApp and automation, and its Standard tier adds unlimited-contact automation, A/B testing and advanced reporting. Brevo Help

**If you're running Shopify/WooCommerce → Klaviyo.**

Klaviyo is much more commerce-centric: customer profiles, behavioral segmentation, abandoned-cart/post-purchase flows and multiple messaging channels are core to the platform. Its free plan also lets a small store start before moving to paid tiers. Klaviyo UK+1

**If you're a YouTuber, consultant, blogger or course creator → Kit.**

Its free tier currently supports up to 10,000 subscribers and includes broadcasts, forms, landing pages, tagging and digital-product selling; paid Creator adds visual automations and unlimited sequences. Kit

**Mailchimp is still good**, especially if you need integrations or already know the platform. Standard includes enhanced automation, behavioral targeting and more advanced segmentation, but its pricing rises with contact count, which is why I wouldn't automatically choose it for a new small business. Mailchimp+1

### My practical ranking for a new small business

**MailerLite → Brevo → Mailchimp** for a normal service/SaaS/local business.

For **e-commerce**, I'd instead start with **Klaviyo**. For a **creator/newsletter business**, I'd start with **Kit**.

And I would **not start with HubSpot** purely for email marketing. Its higher-level marketing suite is far more capable, but Marketing + Content Professional currently starts around **$900/month plus onboarding**, making it overkill for most small businesses unless you're deliberately building your sales and CRM operation around HubSpot. HubSpot

If you tell me what kind of business you're building, your approximate subscriber count, and whether you need **automations, cold outreach, ecommerce or just newsletters**, I can narrow this to the **best 2–3 platforms for your exact use case**.

For a small business in **2026**, these are the platforms I’d shortlist:

| Platform | Best for | Why it stands out | Main drawback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MailerLite** | **Most small businesses** | Easy to use, strong email builder, automations, forms, landing pages and websites | Free plan is now quite small |
| **Brevo** | **Best value / service businesses** | Email + SMS + WhatsApp + CRM; pricing is relatively friendly | Email design/UI isn't quite as polished |
| **Klaviyo** | **E-commerce / Shopify** | Excellent purchase-data segmentation, abandoned-cart flows and revenue attribution | Can become expensive as your list grows |
| **ActiveCampaign** | **Advanced automation** | Powerful workflows, segmentation, CRM and conditional logic | More complicated than most small businesses need |
| **Kit** | **Creators/newsletters** | Excellent subscriber tagging, sequences, digital products and creator tools | Less suited to traditional retail/local businesses |
| **Mailchimp** | **General-purpose / integrations** | Mature ecosystem, lots of templates and integrations | Often poorer value as contacts grow |

### My picks

**🥇 MailerLite — best overall for a typical small business**

If you're running a consultancy, agency, SaaS, local business, website, course business or simple online store, I'd probably start here. The UI is straightforward and you get email campaigns, automation, landing pages, forms, websites and digital-product tools in one system. MailerLite+1

One important change: MailerLite revised its pricing in June 2026. Its current free tier is only **250 active subscribers and 2,500 emails/month**, although it now includes more functionality such as templates and several automations. MailerLite

**🥈 Brevo — best if price and multichannel communication matter**

Brevo is particularly attractive if you want **email + SMS + WhatsApp + basic CRM** instead of just newsletters. Its Free plan allows **300 emails/day** and storage for up to **100,000 contacts**; Starter begins around **$9/month**, while Standard starts around **$18/month** and adds unlimited-contact marketing automation, A/B testing and advanced reporting. Brevo Help

That's a very compelling structure for a business with a reasonably large contact database that doesn't email everyone constantly.

**🥉 Klaviyo — choose this if you're serious about e-commerce**

For Shopify/e-commerce, Klaviyo is much more than an email sender. It connects customer behaviour, purchases, segments, automated flows and revenue attribution. Its current free tier covers up to **250 active profiles and 500 emails/month**. Klaviyo UK

For a conventional small business, though, I'd rather use MailerLite or Brevo and save the complexity/cost.

**ActiveCampaign — for sophisticated automation**

This is the one I'd choose when requirements sound like:

> “If customer does X, but hasn't done Y in seven days, belongs to segment Z, has spent more than $500, and opened the previous campaign, trigger this sequence and update the CRM.”

It supports multi-step automation, increasingly advanced segmentation, CRM/e-commerce integrations, conditional content and other higher-end features. It currently offers a 14-day trial. ActiveCampaign

Excellent software, but probably overkill for someone who only needs newsletters, welcome sequences and lead nurturing.

**Kit — best for creators, bloggers and newsletter businesses**

Kit is unusually generous for audience-building: its Free plan currently supports **up to 10,000 subscribers**, unlimited broadcasts, landing pages/forms, tagging and segmentation. Its Creator tier is currently **$33/month for 1,000 subscribers** and adds unlimited visual automations and sequences. Kit

I'd strongly consider it for a personal brand, paid newsletter, course creator or digital-product business.

**Mailchimp — still good, but no longer my automatic default**

Mailchimp remains extremely established and easy to integrate with other software. Its current advertised starting prices are around **$13/month for Essentials** and **$20/month for Standard**, depending on contacts and billing conditions. Mailchimp

Its biggest advantage is ecosystem and familiarity rather than value. For a brand-new small business, I'd generally check MailerLite and Brevo before paying for Mailchimp.

### So which should you actually choose?

For **90% of ordinary small businesses**, I'd narrow it to:

**MailerLite** → newsletters + marketing automation + landing pages

**Brevo** → email + CRM + SMS/WhatsApp and cost-conscious growth

**Klaviyo** → e-commerce

**ActiveCampaign** → complex automation

**Kit** → creator/newsletter business

If you're starting from scratch and haven't told me anything else about the business, **I'd start with MailerLite**. It's the best balance of capability, simplicity and room to grow.

If you tell me **what type of business you're building, roughly how many contacts you expect, and whether you're selling products/services**, I can narrow these down to **2 platforms and compare their actual cost at 1K, 5K and 10K subscribers**.
